slices.name: ws08-01-open-the-record-and-the-creation-rules
slices.brief:
Open WS08 in the record and build the creation rules, the one place the server and the pages ask who may create an event, who may set a fee above $0, who may name a director and who may delete a draft. No handler changes in this step; nothing a visitor sees changes.

Where this starts. The branch is redesign/ws08-creation-roles, cut from main after the Phase 0 public-answer trim has merged (its branch is phase0/public-answer-trim, uncommitted work on top of b7c11e6 as of Tuesday, November 3, 2026; main is 27fe278). If the trim has not merged when this step starts: cut the branch from main as it is, build this step on it, and merge phase0/public-answer-trim into the branch before step 2 starts (step 2 adds to a list the trim creates, MANAGER_ONLY_TOURNAMENT_KEYS in domain/contracts/events.ts). Checkpoint J's pull request opens only after the trim's own pull request has merged into main, so it carries none of the trim's commits and none of its review. The owner of the repository does the cut and the merge; the step never runs git itself.

1. domain/events/creation.ts (new, zod-free, no import from functions/, src/ or domain/contracts; a type import from ./sections is fine; test/unit/domain-boundaries.test.ts lines 70 to 86 fail anything else). Exports, with these exact names and signatures:
   - export type CreationGrant = 'admin' | 'president' | 'standing_director' | 'club_rep' | 'none'
   - export interface CreationPerson { grant: CreationGrant; memberId: string; repClubId: string | null }. repClubId is the club a club_rep manages by role (member.role club_rep with a club_id), null for everyone else; the right it carries holds whatever the grant, which is how a club rep who holds the President seat keeps every right Q2 leaves club reps.
   - export interface CreationEvent { clubId: string | null; createdBy: string | null }
   - export function canCreate(person: CreationPerson, clubId: string | null, rolesOn: boolean): boolean. In both states: admin any club or none; a person with repClubId that club only (clubId equal to person.repClubId, never null). With rolesOn true also: president and standing_director, clubId null only (their events are LCA-run: Q37 for the standing director, and the table's membership row, "their events are LCA-run", for the president). Everyone else false, so with rolesOn false the president and the standing director are refused.
   - export function canChargeFees(person: CreationPerson, event: CreationEvent, rolesOn: boolean): boolean. With rolesOn false: true for everyone (today anyone requireTournamentManager admits may set a fee). With rolesOn true: true for admin, president, standing_director and club_rep (D24's list), false for none. The event argument is read now only so the Phase 4 member-event rule (every fee $0 on a member-created event) and WS09's representatives have their place; nothing in it changes the answer yet.
   - export function canAssignDirectors(person: CreationPerson, event: CreationEvent, rolesOn: boolean): boolean. Admin always; event.clubId not null and equal to person.repClubId (today's club rep rule, whatever the grant); with rolesOn true also president when event.createdBy is person.memberId; otherwise false (a standing director never, D21).
   - export function canDeleteDraft(person: CreationPerson, event: CreationEvent & { isVisible: number; entries: number }, rolesOn: boolean): boolean. Admin always. Otherwise only with rolesOn true, when event.createdBy is person.memberId, canCreate(person, event.clubId, true) still holds (the grant that let them create), event.isVisible is 0 and event.entries is 0.
   - export function lcaAffiliateAllowed(event: CreationEvent): boolean. Returns true for every event now (D23: every event gets the rating report stage; no member-created event exists until Phase 4, which adds the one case that answers false). Built here because it costs one line and the console part reads it.
   - export const FEES_NEED_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT = 'Entry fees need a payout account first. Until then, your event can run at $0.' (the server's refusal for D24, the panel's title and its last sentence; step 4 answers it and step 10 shows it).
   - export const LCA_RUN_ONLY = "Standing directors and the president create LCA-run events, not a club's." (the create's refusal when either names a club; step 3 answers it).
   - export function feesRaised(before: ReadonlyArray<{ key: string; fees: TierFees }>, after: ReadonlyArray<{ key: string; fees: TierFees }>): boolean, with TierFees a type import from ./sections (regular: number; early and late: number | null). A raise is a rise in what an entrant pays at any tier. For each key in after, regular, early and late are compared with before's entry of the same key, where a missing early or late (null) reads as that section's regular price in both lists (an event with no early price charges regular before its deadline, and one with no late price charges regular after it), and a key with no match in before reads as 0 for every tier. True when any compared price in after is above before's; otherwise false, so an equal list, an echoed answer, a lowered price, a discount that appears and a section left out of after are never raises. Steps 4 and 10 build both lists with tierFees.
   A header comment of at most twelve lines says what the module decides and that the database half is functions/utils/events/creation.ts.

(member.club_id ?? null) : null }. export async function creatorGrant(db: D1Database, tournamentId: string, rolesOn: boolean): Promise<CreationGrant | null>: one statement, SELECT m.id, m.role, m.club_id FROM tournaments t JOIN members m ON m.id = t.created_by WHERE t.id = ?, then creationGrant on the row; null when the event or its creator is missing (step 6 reads it, so the notice's helper never imports functions/utils/admin/members.ts, whose ../supabase import would reach a worker's bundle). slices.name: ws08-02-migration-0059-ticket-kinds-and-review-mark
slices.brief:
Migration 0059: the brief's 00xx_ticket_kinds.sql (lines 1891 to 1895): the ticket kinds and the mark that the D22 notice has gone. Three nullable columns; no table is rebuilt; nothing a visitor sees changes. The trim must be in the tree (merged into main, or merged into the branch by the owner before this step starts), since this step adds to the list the trim created. This step touches about seventeen files (nineteen when the two trim contract tests enumerate the keys) once the Drizzle snapshot, the journal, the trim's tests and the six tests whose figures the new migration moves are counted, so the lead's scout composes its brief from this entry (the plan notes say which steps get one).

1. functions/db/schema.ts. In supportTickets (lines 279 to 296), after number (line 289): kind: text() and aboutId: text('about_id'). In tournaments (lines 68 to 127), after requiresLcaMembership (line 119): reviewNotifiedAt: text('review_notified_at'). Each with a one-line comment (kind: NULL for an ordinary ticket, else listing_report, event_report or payout_request; about_id: the clearinghouse listing or the tournament the ticket is about; review_notified_at: the D22 notice went at this event's first publish, sent only while NULL). No publish_at: it is Phase 2's column (the brief's 00xx_console.sql, line 1910), written only by the setup checklist's Publish step (line 1860), and the console part adds it with its phase. No index.

2. The migration, written with npm run db:generate -- ticket_kinds (migrations/README.md lines 36 to 55): drizzle-kit writes three ALTER TABLE ... ADD statements, the script numbers the file 0059 and adds its header, and the new snapshot, drizzle/meta/0008_snapshot.json (drizzle/meta holds 0000 to 0007 on 27fe278), and its entry in drizzle/meta/_journal.json are committed with it. The file is migrations/0059_ticket_kinds.sql holding exactly: ALTER TABLE `support_tickets` ADD `kind` text; ALTER TABLE `support_tickets` ADD `about_id` text; ALTER TABLE `tournaments` ADD `review_notified_at` text; each after a "--> statement-breakpoint" line as drizzle-kit writes them. No REFERENCES, no CHECK, no trigger, no data statement. Add below the generated header a comment of at most six lines saying what each column is for, as 0054's header does (migrations/0054_requires_lca_membership.sql). If the generator cannot run in the container (it needs a terminal only for renames; this has none), write the file by hand in the same shape and run npm run db:generate -- ticket_kinds --custom to record the snapshot; say which in the record.
